title: Trajectory property for sequential contracts
statement: Let $C_1$ be a contract for a machine $M_1$ from entry state $e_1$ to the sole exit state $f_1$, and let $C_2$ be a contract for a machine $M_2$ from entry state $e_2$ to an exit set $X_2$, on the same input and with the same number of work tapes. Suppose a map links the data for $C_1$ to the data for $C_2$ and every eligible endpoint of $C_1$, with its state replaced by $e_2$, satisfies the corresponding $C_2$ precondition. If $R_1$ and $R_2$ hold throughout the trajectories of $C_1$ and $C_2$, respectively, then the sequentially composed contract satisfies, at every time, the disjunction of $R_1$ on the initial phase and $R_2$ on the linked datum and the intermediate endpoint with its state replaced by $e_2$.
hypotheses_covered: C₁ exits at the sole state f₁
C₂ starts at e₂ and exits in X₂
Both machines use the same input and number of work tapes
A data map links C₁ data to C₂ data
Every eligible C₁ endpoint, with state replaced by e₂, satisfies C₂'s precondition
replaced:
Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be contracts for machines $M_1$ and $M_2$ with the same $k$ work
tapes and input alphabet, where $C_1$ exits at a designated state and $C_2$ begins at
its designated entry state. Suppose a link maps each datum for $C_1$ to a datum for
$C_2$, and the endpoint of every admissible $C_1$ run, with its state replaced by the
entry state of $M_2$, satisfies the corresponding $C_2$ precondition. If $C_1$ and $C_2$
satisfy trajectory properties $R_1$ and $R_2$, respectively, then their sequentially
composed contract satisfies, at every time, the disjunction of $R_1$ for the initial
phase and $R_2$ for the linked datum and the intermediate endpoint.
